The list is constructed by considering market capitalization, 3-year historical annual returns, and the current price-to-earnings ratio. Note that this list is tailored to avoid concentration risk by allocating within the 10% limit for any single equity position. ESG concerns flagged for each position are noted, and their potential impacts on the portfolio's risk-adjusted returns are balanced with their expected contributions.

bonds.analysis:
We'll consider 2-year and 5-year Treasuries to maintain a laddered maturity structure and stay within the 10-year duration limit. For the corporate bond segment, we recommend 3-year investment-grade bonds from companies like Microsoft (AA- rated) and Johnson & Johnson (AA-rated). These options have solid credit ratings and durations below 7 years, exceeding the requirement. 
  Our focus is on preserving capital and providing predictable returns, so we prioritize shorter-term investments with lower credit risk. A balanced portfolio will ensure stability while meeting our growth objectives. The maturity ladder allows flexible management and optimal liquidity, especially in the near term. For TIPS, we suggest adding 2-year and 5-year maturities to match the Treasury laddered structure, ensuring diversified returns.

materials.analysis: Historically, gold and silver have demonstrated positive correlation with inflation, offering a hedge against its eroding purchasing power. As inflation expectations rise, the value of these precious metals tends to increase due to their store-of-value characteristics. In this context, we recommend an allocation of 10% to gold and 5% to silver, as they are the most straightforward and directly-protective options. This is based on the rationale that central banks and investors tend to increase demand for gold and silver as a store-of-value when inflation expectations rise, thereby driving up their prices. Furthermore, an investment-grade gold or silver allocation is the simplest, most reliable, and most liquid way to directly hedge against inflation.

payload.analysis:
We've examined suitable Treasuries, corporate bonds, and TIPS for the current market environment, focusing on achieving a balance between short-term liquidity and long-term growth. The laddered maturity structure is crucial, so we'll aim to spread investments across different years. We recommend buying Treasuries and corporate bonds with stable credit ratings to manage risk. TIPS offer inflation protection but generally have lower yields compared to other options.

We propose allocating 20% to 5-year Treasuries (Y) with a credit rating of AA+ (S&P) to lock in short-term liquidity. For a longer-term, stable investment, we suggest allocating 30% to 10-year corporate bonds from companies with credit ratings ranging from BBB+ to A- (S&P). These corporate bonds offer higher yields than Treasuries, while their rating ensures they're less likely to default. Lastly, we recommend allocating 15% to 10-year TIPS with a maturity date in 2-5 years to provide a fixed income stream while adjusting for inflation.

As our portfolio duration is below 7 years, we flag a warning to keep an eye on the overall portfolio duration if new investments push it above 7 years. However, our current recommendations comply with the maximum portfolio duration limit. We suggest spreading maturities across years to maintain the laddered maturity structure. Currently, our allocation plan has a maturity distribution where no year has more than 30% of the total maturity, adhering to the required laddered structure.

The proposed maturity allocation is [0.20, 0.30, 0.15, 0.15, 0.10, 0.10, 0.00] for the 1-year, 2-to-5 years, 6-to-10 years, 11-to-15 years, and 15-to-20 years maturity buckets, respectively. No specific allocations are proposed for the remaining maturity buckets.
